title: Intel Bets on Cheaper AI as Foundry Losses Mount
key_facts: MarketBeat analysis: Intel detailed its GPU D-Series (code-named Crescent Island), an air-cooled inference chip, at the Open Compute Project summit.
Intel's foundry division posted an operating loss of nearly $2.1 billion despite 31% revenue growth.
CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought about 105,000 shares near $95; short interest is about 158 million shares.
Intel suspended its dividend to fund research and factory upgrades.
Intel reports third-quarter earnings on 29 Oct.
The shares are about 20% below September highs and trade at a forward price-to-earnings ratio near 98.
quote_evidence: The company's foundry division posted a nearly $2.1 billion operating loss despite 31% revenue growth, highlighting heavy reliance on new hardware to offset margin pressure.
Intel's current valuation profile presents a complex scenario.
why_it_matters_hint: The D-series is part of Intel's effort to fund its costly factory turnaround.
